# R424 — Current layer-major prefill timer contract

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source and retained-record audit. No build, test, AST, GPU, profiler, process/service action, cleanup, source edit, or unrelated environment scan. Only this report was written.

## Decision

`STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1` is suitable as a separately labeled phase-ranking diagnostic for the current 4K/32K layer-major path, with two limits: each line is one layer's `run_impl` aggregation over its chunks, and the phase values are compute-queue command-end intervals, not kernel-only service. Its mark/fold work adds host API overhead and an existing checked sync lets `fold()` read completed events; it adds no queue drain of its own. Do not treat its output as quiet performance evidence or claim that any label is pure GPU execution.

The current Main record already proves a 32,768-row actual GEN1024/32768 request passed with all 32,767 model tokens resident in the 1,342,136,320-byte GPU residual allocation and zero host residual rows. Its prompt subtotal was 55,568.811 ms, including 14,961.143 ms in the 24,576 checked expert-upload calls (50,292,326,400 logical bytes). The 1,023-row request had 14,628.250 ms of the same upload span and 17,027.230 ms total. These are retained diagnostics, not qualified speed samples. The timer can classify layer/chunk compute phases on a future identical source/build/input run; it cannot explain the upload span because that upload occurs in `run_layer_major` before each `run_impl` timer is constructed.

## Timer lifecycle and aggregation

`Prefill::run()` dispatches the layer-major request to `run_layer_major()` (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:1417-1420`). The outer loop processes each model layer and calls `run_impl()` once with `LB=layer, LE=layer+1` (`1515-1558`). Thus it constructs 48 independent local `PfTimer` objects. Inside each `run_impl`, the chunk loop runs from `c0=0` to `n` in steps of `m.T` and records `kPfStart` on each chunk (`1641-1653`). In the retained GEN record, 32,767 tokens used 8 chunks at `T=4096`; therefore each one-layer call's timer spans 8 chunk bodies, not the whole 48-layer pass.

`PfTimer::mark()` records a timing event on `m.cs`; `fold()` iterates adjacent marks, queries elapsed `command_end` timestamps, accumulates the interval under the earlier mark's phase, and retains the last mark for the next interval (`1367-1410`). The common MoE path calls the existing checked `stream_sync(m.cs)` before `pt.fold()` (`2284`); at the end of `run_impl`, another pre-existing checked terminal compute sync precedes the final fold (`3408-3413`). In this one-layer schedule, the timer has one fold at each MoE synchronization encountered in the 8 chunks plus the terminal fold; actual fold count follows the current layer's control flow. The fold reads completed mark events and does not synchronize the queue itself. It allocates timing events only as needed and reuses them after folding.

The output omits labels whose accumulated interval is zero and prints one `strata prefill timing:` line per `run_impl`, with that layer call's `n`, the sum of its accumulated labeled intervals (`GPU timeline`), whole `run_impl` wall interval, and the shared `stats_.ms_experts_host` subtotal (`3421-3432`). The second line prints host chunk setup/sync/after-chunk and PLE wall aggregates. A third line reports timer host API overhead: marker calls, newly created events, fold calls, and completed intervals (`3431-3433`). `mark_host_ms` and `fold_host_ms` are explanatory host-wall counters, not subtracted from the timeline. Phase percentages divide by the sum of labeled command-end intervals, not by request wall.

## Meaning and limits of a phase interval

The interval is the difference between two recorded events' `command_end` timestamps on the in-order compute queue. It includes any commands submitted between the marks and any queue idle time before the later mark's completion. For example, if host grouping delays the next submission, that delay can appear under the earlier open label; if work waits on a copy event from the separate copy queue, the wait is represented by the later compute command's completion interval. The reported label is therefore an ordered queue interval, not the service time of one named kernel. `wait copy` is still a useful queue-wait clue, not a standalone PCIe measurement.

The timer does not wrap the outer expert-upload loop. That loop occurs before `run_impl`: for each layer it resolves 512 source pointers and calls checked synchronous `gpu::copy` for each expert, then updates `stats_.ms_experts_host` (`1515-1540`). The output's `host staging` field repeats that cumulative counter on every layer's timer line; it is not that line's per-layer upload duration and should not be summed across the 48 lines. The separate outer trace is optional `STRATA_TRACE` and must not be presented as a quiet timing run.

## Queue and event support

`PfTimer::mark()` passes `m.cs`, the compute stream, not a copy-only stream. `gpu::event_record()` rejects timing events only for copy-only streams, then uses `submit_profiling_tag(queue)` for timing events (`src/core/gpu.cpp:363-383`). `event_elapsed_ms()` reads `command_end` for both tags and converts the difference from nanoseconds to milliseconds (`405-418`). The compute queue is created in-order. `STRATA_PREFILL_SERVICE_EVENTS` only controls queue `enable_profiling` in `runtime_queue_properties` (`src/core/device.cpp:197-201`); the timer's explicit profiling-tag path is not gated on that environment flag. Runtime/build support for the tag and actual nonzero/monotonic timings still has to succeed in the diagnostic run. If event creation/record/query fails, `publication::require` makes that diagnostic request fail; do not suppress the timer error or treat partial phases as valid.

The timer code creates events lazily during the first marks, so creation allocation/API cost occurs in the instrumented call and is counted in `mark_host_ms`; subsequent marks reuse them. It destroys its event objects with the local timer on return. The diagnostic does not retain a full trace or raw event timeline.

## Recommendation for the Main diagnostic

Use one bounded diagnostic run after the unchanged Main path is closed and the official status is known. Reuse the same phase4k executable, fixed GEN 4K capacity, all-GPU 32K input, model/session reset, `max_new=1`, identical request packet and all recorded environment values; set only `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING=1`. Capture the 48 per-layer timing lines, corresponding bounded wall/quality result and timer-overhead lines. Keep its status `diagnostic_engine_timings_only` and `performance_eligible=false`. Do not run simultaneous profiler/copy tracing, do not turn on service events, and do not use this result as an unchanged quiet benchmark sample. Because the timer cannot split the pre-`run_impl` uploads, retain the existing outer `ms_experts_host` number unchanged and use a later source/copy wall split only if Main chooses to make that diagnostic edit.

Prior to drawing a critical-path conclusion, check that all 48 layer lines are present, each has finite nonnegative timeline and wall values, timer errors are absent, and the successful output/first-row hash matches its qualified same-input control. Compare the largest phase labels only as ranking evidence. Queue intervals can overlap with host work on other threads and are not additive to enclosing wall; never sum phase values over all layers and call that whole-request time. No production timer/source edit is indicated by this audit.

## Measured context consulted

Main's retained record: `/home/yayoi/.local/state/strata-sycl/post-reboot-tuning-20261007/main-layer-major-phase4k-prefix32k-first-row-root-v1/record.json`, read as a closed record (`active=false`, `complete=true`, `passed=true`). It identifies source revision `8b48d17c99b70d32781f9f5b056602a598a37b1c`, binary SHA-256 `aa35f0f4f2e37608462b0884c8e47df3dd79f19c626715f5dbfd5704579ed881`, requested 32,768 GPU rows, actual 32,767 GPU residual rows and zero host residual rows, and no performance samples. The two request rows are:

- 1,023 tokens, one chunk: internal total 17,027.230 ms; checked source+upload wall 14,628.250 ms; streamed 24,576 blobs.
- 32,767 tokens, eight chunks: internal total 55,568.811 ms; checked source+upload wall 14,961.143 ms; streamed 24,576 blobs.

This is not a 32K throughput claim. The record explicitly marks quality qualification false, `performance_eligible=false`, `performance_samples=[]`; its full physical 262K gate was not qualified. Use only the timer contract and already-recorded numerical/operational status, not its wall values as a speed baseline.

R420 was consulted at `research-prefill-span-traffic-roofline-contract-round420-v1.txt`; it independently establishes the upload wall scope, source-vs-transfer caveat, and that this run does not have a complete leaf-service profile. The current Main run remains authoritative for actual prompt facts.
